title: Lumen Quarterly Autumn issue: grade ten mixed-light feature photos to one warm-editorial house look, tame an off-brand oversaturated hero, vectorize the masthead, and data-merge one press-ready feature opener per story

source.reference: Graphic Design Aligned with Brand Standards

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com brand-standards brief (the client wants every piece to stay 'strictly inside my existing brand guidelines' and supplies 'the full style guide - logo lock-ups, colour palette, typography rules, imagery tone, even sample layouts', requiring that 'each design feels cohesive with the rest of the brand'). Laundered to a fictional independent arts-and-culture magazine, 'Lumen Quarterly' (published by the fictional 'Lumen House Press') - no real company, publication, person, product or trademark is named, and the house typefaces are described by role ('the house display serif', 'the house grotesque sans') rather than by any real font name. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the killed version was an ANALYZE audit that only emitted a .md/.json findings report and whose 'defects' (a ~5% hue delta, a 104% stretch) were unmeasurable by the connector and were even printed into the brief - so an agent scored full marks without looking. This rebuild inverts it into the actual production job the brand-standards brief rewards and that the connector can genuinely do: the incoming Autumn 2026 feature photography was shot by several contributors across mixed lighting and does NOT read as one magazine, so the agent must (a) neutralise every frame to the in-frame grey card and pull the whole set onto ONE warm-editorial house look the guide demands, (b) bring one hero photo whose oversaturated prop breaks the 'no oversaturation' imagery rule back into the editorial palette with a masked in-family recolor, (c) prep-and-vectorize the scanned masthead lock-up so it prints crisp, and (d) merge the story roster into the client's authored single-record InDesign feature-opener template and export a press-ready 300 DPI issue, one opener page per story. The coral brand accent lives as typography inside the authored template (pull-quotes set in the house coral), so no photo is asked to hit a brand hex. Everything is produced by the connector from supplied authored inputs; nothing is generative and nothing is a findings report.
one_line_ask: Take ten mixed-lighting Autumn-issue feature photos (each carrying an in-frame grey card), neutralise every frame to its card and grade the whole set to one warm-editorial house look, bring the ceramics hero's oversaturated red bowls back into the editorial palette with a masked in-family recolor without flattening the glaze, prep-and-vectorize the scanned masthead lock-up, then data-merge the client's authored feature-opener template against the story roster to export a press-ready 300 DPI feature opener for every story.
full_brief:
Lumen Quarterly is a small independent arts-and-culture magazine. We are closing the Autumn 2026 issue and our feature photography is a mess of mismatched light: the stories were shot by different contributors on different days - some under warm tungsten in studios and workshops, some by cold north-facing windows, one flat and underexposed in a dim archive, one blown-out on a rooftop at noon - so straight out of the folder the issue does not read as ONE magazine, and our board rejects issues that look stitched together. Our brand's imagery rule is that all photography is warm, editorial and consistently graded, with no cold or blue casts and no oversaturation. To give you something honest to balance against, every photographer left a photographic 18% grey card at the edge of frame. Here is the job.

First, the set has to become one room. Bring every one of the ten feature photos to a consistent look by neutralising each frame to the grey card it carries - the card must read as a clean neutral grey in your finished frame - and then settle the whole set onto a single warm-editorial house look: a shared white point, a gentle warm editorial tone in the highlights and shadows, restrained (never punchy) saturation. Do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch: a warm tungsten frame and a cold window frame need opposite white-balance moves to arrive at the same place, and an underexposed archive frame and an overexposed rooftop frame need opposite exposure moves. Be careful with the sound-artist forest frame - it was shot under flat neutral overcast, so its grey card already reads neutral and the woodland genuinely is cool and misty; the warm editorial feeling on that frame must come from the shared TONE you apply to the whole set, not from shoving its white balance warm - if you 'warm out an imagined blue cast' there you will push its neutral card off-neutral and turn a true grey day orange. The warmth is a house tone laid on every frame equally; the white-balance correction is per-frame and driven by each card. When you are done, tell us the white-balance and exposure move you dialed on each frame so we can confirm the set was matched, not eyeballed.

Second, one photo breaks the palette. The ceramics feature ('The Slow Kiln') hero has a stack of glazed bowls in a hot, almost fluorescent tomato-red that reads garish against our warm-editorial palette and trips the 'no oversaturation' rule. Bring just those bowls down into the editorial range - a deeper, softer terracotta in the same red-earth family, muted and darkened, NOT a jump to some far-off hue - and it has to sit under the real glaze: the sheen, the throwing rings and the shadow inside each bowl must survive. Only the bowls - do not desaturate the potter, the kiln or the rest of the frame, and no flat painted-on colour.

Third, our masthead lock-up only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper and it prints fuzzy. Get it clean and razor-sharp as vector art for the opener furniture.

Finally, build the issue. We have hand-built the InDesign feature-opener template with the real placeholder fields - headline, standfirst, pull-quote (which sets in our house coral accent), byline and folio - plus an image frame for the story's hero photo and a masthead frame, and we are giving you the story roster. Merge them so every story gets its own single-page opener with its copy bound and its matching graded hero placed, then hand back a press-ready ~300 DPI A4 PDF of the openers, with the lead feature ('The Slow Kiln') running as the opening page so the editor sees it first. Bind the copy verbatim from the roster - do not rewrite our headlines or standfirsts. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set matched to one warm-editorial white point and tone; the ceramics bowls softened within their own colour family with the glaze intact; the masthead a clean crisp vector; and exactly one finished opener page per roster row.

inputs.name: F01_slow_kiln_ceramics_hero.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal editorial magazine feature photograph, raw unretouched full-frame-camera look, ~4200px long edge: a ceramicist at a pottery wheel in a working studio, and in the foreground a stack of glazed stoneware bowls in a HOT, almost fluorescent tomato-red glaze that is clearly oversaturated and too punchy. Warm tungsten studio lighting with a strong amber cast, real clay dust, wheel splatter, throwing rings and glossy glaze sheen with visible highlights and interior shadow in each bowl. A photographic 18% neutral grey card rests flat at the lower-left edge of the frame as a white-balance reference. Candid documentary editorial style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU F01, warm tungsten session and the RECOLOR hero. Two things happen here: the warm cast must be COOLED to neutralise its grey card onto the shared white point, and the oversaturated tomato-red bowls must be brought into the warm-editorial palette by a MASKED in-family deepen-and-mute (small hue nudge toward terracotta + saturation/luminance drop) that keeps the glaze sheen and interior shadow - not a whole-image tint and not a flat fill. ~4200px so the 300 DPI A4 opener crop is a downscale, never an upscale.

inputs.name: F02_paper_cities_papercut.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal editorial feature photograph, raw unretouched look, ~4000px long edge: a papercut artist bent over an intricate layered paper cityscape on a workbench, shot by a cold north-facing window with a distinct blue-cyan daylight cast, slightly flat and marginally underexposed, frame tilted about 3 degrees. Real paper fibre, blade, cutting mat and soft window shadow. A photographic 18% neutral grey card sits at the lower-right edge of frame as a white-balance reference. Candid documentary editorial style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU F02, cool window session, tilted ~3deg (auto_straighten has work). Its grey card is blue-cast: the correct move is to WARM the white balance to neutral - the OPPOSITE sign to the tungsten frames - then take the shared warm-editorial house tone. Tests that the agent reasons per-frame, not one blanket correction.

inputs.name: F03_field_recordings_forest.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal editorial feature photograph, raw unretouched look, ~4100px long edge: a sound artist crouched with a microphone rig in a misty temperate forest, genuinely cool blue-green woodland light under FLAT NEUTRAL OVERCAST (no strong cast either way), balanced neutral exposure. Real moss, wet bark, drifting mist, muted natural greens. A photographic 18% neutral grey card sits at the lower edge of frame as a white-balance reference and already reads close to neutral. Candid documentary editorial style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU F03, the NEUTRAL-CARD TRAP. Shot under neutral overcast, so its in-frame grey card is already essentially neutral and the correct white-balance move is to HOLD (no meaningful temp/tint shift); the warm-editorial feeling must come only from the SHARED house tone applied to every frame. A naive agent that batch-applies the tungsten frames' 'warm it up' correction, or tries to 'warm out an imagined blue cast', pushes the neutral card orange and destroys a genuinely cool, true-to-life grey day. The decision must be driven by THIS card.

inputs.name: F04_letterpress_workshop.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal editorial feature photograph, raw unretouched look, ~4000px long edge: a printer inking a cast-iron letterpress in a workshop, warm tungsten overhead work-light with a strong orange cast, frame tilted about 4 degrees. Real metal type, ink rollers, paper stock and machine grease. A photographic 18% neutral grey card rests at the frame edge as a white-balance reference. Candid documentary editorial style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU F04, warm tungsten session, tilted ~4deg. Cool the white balance to neutralise the card to the shared white point; distinct numbers from F01 because the light and exposure differ. Straighten before grading.

inputs.name: F05_bookbinder_archive.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal editorial feature photograph, raw unretouched look, ~4000px long edge: a bookbinder stitching a text block at a bench in a dim archive, warm low tungsten light, clearly UNDEREXPOSED and flat so the shadows muddy toward black. Real thread, bone folder, leather and aged paper. A photographic 18% neutral grey card sits at the frame edge as a white-balance reference. Candid documentary editorial style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU F05, warm and underexposed. The dominant move is TONAL - LIFT exposure and open the shadows to reach the set brightness while holding the black point off zero - plus a modest warm-to-neutral WB nudge to the card. A different problem from the pure cast frames.

inputs.name: F06_jazz_club_portrait.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal editorial feature photograph, raw unretouched look, ~4100px long edge: a double-bass player in a small jazz club, warm tungsten stage wash with an amber cast, moderate contrast, level. Real instrument varnish, stage haze and skin tones. A photographic 18% neutral grey card sits at the frame edge as a white-balance reference. Candid documentary editorial style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU F06, warm tungsten, level. Cool the white balance to the shared white point and protect skin tones from going grey; take the shared house tone. Close to F01/F04 in cast but its own exposure, so its reported numbers must not be copied.

inputs.name: F07_coastal_architecture.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal editorial feature photograph, raw unretouched look, ~4200px long edge: a modernist concrete house on a cliff under bright cool coastal daylight with a clear blue-cyan cast, slightly overbright, frame tilted about 3 degrees. Real concrete texture, glass reflections, sea and sky. A photographic 18% neutral grey card sits at the frame edge as a white-balance reference. Candid documentary editorial style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU F07, cool daylight, tilted ~3deg, a touch bright. WARM the white balance to neutral AND pull exposure down toward the set brightness - a two-axis correction opposite in sign to the tungsten frames on WB and opposite to the underexposed archive on exposure. Straighten first.

inputs.name: F08_rooftop_garden_noon.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal editorial feature photograph, raw unretouched look, ~4000px long edge: an urban rooftop kitchen garden at midday, near-neutral but very bright noon light, OVEREXPOSED with blown-risk highlights on pale flowers and watering can, level. Real soil, foliage, herb texture. A photographic 18% neutral grey card sits at the frame edge as a white-balance reference. Candid documentary editorial style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU F08, overexposed and near-neutral. The dominant move is to RECOVER highlights and pull exposure DOWN to the set brightness while neutralising the small residual cast on the card - opposite exposure direction to the underexposed archive frame. Protect the blown flowers.

inputs.name: F09_textile_weaver.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal editorial feature photograph, raw unretouched look, ~4100px long edge: a weaver at a floor loom threaded with naturally-dyed wool, cool soft window daylight with a blue cast, frame tilted about 3 degrees. Real wool fibre, loom timber and the coloured warp threads. A photographic 18% neutral grey card sits at the frame edge as a white-balance reference. Candid documentary editorial style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU F09, cool window, tilted ~3deg. Warm the white balance to neutralise the card, but hold the naturally-dyed wool hues true (do not oversaturate the warp) while taking the shared restrained house tone. Straighten first.

inputs.name: F10_market_still_life.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal editorial feature photograph, raw unretouched look, ~4000px long edge: a still-life of autumn produce and preserves on a market stall under MIXED light - warm stall bulbs on one side, cool open shade on the other - level, moderate exposure. Real skins, jars, labels and woven baskets. A photographic 18% neutral grey card sits at the frame edge as a white-balance reference. Candid documentary editorial style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU F10, mixed light. Neutralise to the card (a compromise WB that resolves the mixed cast) and take the shared house tone; its correction resembles no other frame exactly - the batch cannot be solved with one setting.

inputs.name: lumen_masthead_lockup_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'Lumen Quarterly' masthead lock-up inked on slightly warm off-white textured paper: the word 'LUMEN' in a high-contrast serif display face with 'QUARTERLY' set small and letter-spaced beneath it, deep navy ink. Rendered as a real scan - the paper is a warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 degrees) on the scan bed, there is generous paper margin around it, and the edges are a touch soft as a flatbed scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it vectorizes crisply.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, ~2deg rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize fed the raw file would trace the paper rectangle and bake in the skew - forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, crisp/drop the off-white ground, crop to the mark, knock to transparency, THEN vectorize. gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible lettering.

inputs.name: lumen_feature_opener_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A4 portrait magazine feature-opener - ONE story per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<headline>>, <<standfirst>>, <<pull_quote>>, <<byline>>, <<folio>>, with the <<pull_quote>> frame styled in the house coral accent and the <<headline>> in the house display serif and body/standfirst in the house grotesque sans (type and the coral accent baked into the template, NOT chosen by the agent). It must also carry ONE image frame wired to an @-prefixed image-path column (@hero) for the story's graded hero photo, and a masthead frame wired to a second @-prefixed column (@masthead) for the vectorized lock-up. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and both image columns actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real <<fields>> plus genuine @-image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW - so a single-record feature opener is the correct, connector-doable shape (a multi-page magazine flow or an N-up contact sheet is impossible here). The house coral accent and the two typefaces are the client's brand, baked into the template, so the agent never has to hit a brand hex on a photo or pick a font. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd would not bind.

inputs.name: lumen_story_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (client-supplied): a 10-row data-merge CSV, one row per Autumn feature story, with text columns headline, standfirst, pull_quote, byline, folio and TWO @-prefixed image-path columns: @hero (resolves to that story's graded feature photo, e.g. @F01_slow_kiln_graded.jpg) and @masthead (resolves to the vectorized lumen_masthead.svg, the SAME file on every row). Header names must exactly match the template's <<fields>> and its @hero / @masthead frames. Rows are ordered so the lead feature 'The Slow Kiln' is row 1 (and therefore the opening page of the merged PDF), followed by Paper Cities, Field Recordings and the other seven, each with a real editorial headline, a one-to-two-line standfirst, a short pull-quote, a contributor byline and the folio string.
inputs.realism_notes: The @hero column is the binding contract: the agent must point each row at its own graded photo so the one-file-per-row [T] merge drops the correct hero into that story's opener; @masthead points every row at the produced SVG. Ten rows fixes the page=row acceptance gate, and row 1 (The Slow Kiln) becomes page 1 of the merged PDF - the 'lead opener' is the first page of the single exported document, never a separately exported per-record file. Text-only document_merge_data_vector is explicitly the WRONG tool - it cannot bind either image column.

outputs.name: neutralised_card_masters_x10
outputs.spec: The ten RETAINED card-BEARING neutralisation masters (f01_neutral, f02_neutral, f03_neutral, f04_neutral, f05_neutral, f06_neutral, f07_neutral, f08_neutral, f09_neutral, f10_neutral) - each the full-frame frame AFTER its per-frame white-balance/exposure neutralisation to its own in-frame 18% grey card plus the single shared warm-editorial house tone, with the grey card STILL IN FRAME (uncropped, full-res, before any downscale crop). These are the retained/exported neutrality-evidence files and the source the card-out delivered crops are cut from. Acceptance (grader-checked ON THESE card-bearing masters, where the reference card still exists): every frame's in-frame grey card reads a clean neutral within a tight per-channel tolerance and the whole set resolves to ONE shared white point with the single shared warm-editorial tone; no white clipped to 255 / no black crushed to 0; the corrections must be NON-identical across the warm vs cool vs neutral vs over/under-exposed frames (identical reported numbers are a fail). Accompanied by the applied-parameters sheet the agent authors: per frame, the white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure move it dialed, plus the single shared house tone applied to all ten. DELIVERABLE 1 (retained neutralisation masters - the grey-card neutrality gate is graded HERE, on the card-bearing file).

outputs.name: graded_feature_photos_x10
outputs.spec: Ten Autumn-issue feature photos (F01..F10) - the DELIVERED crops cut from the retained card-bearing masters (neutralised_card_masters_x10), each cropped to the opener image-frame ratio so the in-frame grey card is fully OUT of frame, straightened where tilted (F02/F04/F07/F09), downscale-only from the ~4000-4200px source, >=300 effective DPI at the A4 opener placement, sRGB JPEG, carrying the same shared warm-editorial house look as their masters. Acceptance (grader-checked ON THESE crops): the grey card is fully EXCLUDED from every delivered crop (a card-EXCLUSION check only - grey-card neutrality is NOT graded on these files, it is graded on neutralised_card_masters_x10 where the card still exists); no white clipped to 255 / no black crushed to 0. These are the @hero photos placed into the story openers. DELIVERABLE 1 (delivered card-out crops).

outputs.name: F01_slow_kiln_graded.jpg
outputs.spec: The ceramics hero from the matched set, additionally carrying the masked in-family recolor: the oversaturated tomato-red glazed bowls brought down to a deeper, muted terracotta in the same red-earth family via a masked luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl pass pair (a small within-family hue nudge plus a saturation/luminance drop - an in-band deepen-and-mute, NO near-complementary rotation) riding the bowls' existing luminosity so the glaze sheen, throwing rings and interior shadow stay natural, and the potter/kiln/rest of the frame untouched. This is the @hero for the Slow Kiln opener. Part of DELIVERABLE 1.

outputs.name: lumen_masthead.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the 'Lumen Quarterly' masthead lock-up, traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark and knocked to transparency - razor-sharp at opener scale with no captured off-white paper ground and no baked-in skew. Bound to the @masthead frame on every opener. DELIVERABLE 2.

outputs.name: Lumen_Autumn2026_Feature_Openers.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly ten press-ready A4 portrait feature-opener pages - ONE single-record opener per roster row (page-count = row-count = 10) - produced by merging lumen_story_roster.csv into the authored lumen_feature_opener_template.indd via document_merge_data_layout and exported as ONE multi-page document with document_render_layout. Roster row order sets page order, so the lead feature 'The Slow Kiln' is row 1 and therefore the opening page of this PDF - the editor's 'lead opener' is page 1 of this single exported document, NOT a separately exported per-record file. Each opener binds its headline/standfirst/pull-quote/byline/folio verbatim from the roster (pull-quote in the house coral accent baked into the template), drops that story's graded hero through @hero and the vectorized lock-up through @masthead, at ~300 DPI. Acceptance gate: page-count == row-count == 10 (a collapsed or empty-frame merge fails this); each placed hero renders >=300 DPI at the A4 trim. DELIVERABLE 3.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: F01_slow_kiln_ceramics_hero.jpg, F02_paper_cities_papercut.jpg, F03_field_recordings_forest.jpg, F04_letterpress_workshop.jpg, F05_bookbinder_archive.jpg, F06_jazz_club_portrait.jpg, F07_coastal_architecture.jpg, F08_rooftop_garden_noon.jpg, F09_textile_weaver.jpg, F10_market_still_life.jpg, lumen_masthead_lockup_scan.png, lumen_feature_opener_template.indd, lumen_story_roster.csv
connector_workflow.note: Load the ten raw feature photos, the masthead scan, the authored feature-opener .indd template and the story roster CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream step has real asset references. Single upload - plumbing, not the difficulty.

F01 ceramics (warm tungsten). COOL the temperature and set tint so the in-frame grey card reads neutral at the shared white point, then lay on the shared warm-editorial house tone (gentle warm highlights/shadows, restrained vibrance, blacks held off zero). Reason the exact temp/tint/exposure to THIS card - do not reuse another frame's numbers. Authored from primitives, not a preset, not auto_tone. Report the move. Feeds the recolor branch, so keep it full-res before cropping.

Semantically select ONLY the stack of red glazed bowls ('the stack of bright red glazed ceramic bowls in the foreground') so the recolor is confined to them and never touches the potter, kiln or studio. Returns a maskURI. A real object selection, not a hue/coordinate pick.

Masked recolor pass 1 (base + bowls mask): keep the bowls in the red-earth family but nudge the hot tomato-red toward deeper terracotta - a small within-band hue move (well under ~60 deg, staying in red/earth; NOT a near-complementary rotation) plus a first luminance drop, letting the bowls' existing luminosity carry the glaze sheen, throwing rings and interior shadow. Confined to the mask. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image and image_fill_area is flat solid dead-fill - both wrong here.

Masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): trim the red-band SATURATION down and settle the luminance so the bowls land on a muted editorial terracotta that respects the 'no oversaturation' rule - a deepen-and-mute in the same hue family, not a swing to a new hue - still riding the original luminosity so the glaze stays glossy and real.

Crop the finished ceramics hero to the opener image-frame ratio (3:2 landscape), grey card out of frame, resize downscale-only to the placement size (>=300 DPI at the A4 opener). onSubjectClipping='extract', never canvas-extend/upscale. DELIVERABLE F01_slow_kiln_graded.jpg and the @hero for the Slow Kiln row.
F02 papercut is tilted ~3deg - level it before grading so the later crop is true. (Only the tilted frames F02/F04/F07/F09 get straightened; deciding which is part of the job.)

F02 papercut (cool north-window, blue cast, slightly flat/under). WARM the temperature to neutralise the grey card to the shared white point - the OPPOSITE sign to the tungsten frames - lift a touch to the set brightness, then lay on the SAME shared warm-editorial house tone. Distinct numbers from F01 because the light differs. Report the move.
Crop to the opener ratio, grey card out, downscale-only to the placement size. @hero for the Paper Cities row.

F03 forest - THE NEUTRAL-CARD TRAP. Shot under flat neutral overcast, so its grey card is ALREADY neutral: HOLD the white balance (no meaningful temp/tint shift) and match only exposure/brightness to the set, then lay on the SAME shared warm-editorial house TONE that every frame receives - the warmth here is the house tone, NOT a WB push. A naive agent that batch-applies the tungsten 'warm it up' correction, or 'warms out an imagined blue cast', pushes this neutral card orange and wrecks a genuinely cool grey day. Report that WB was held and only the shared tone applied.
Crop to the opener ratio, grey card out, downscale-only. @hero for the Field Recordings row.
F04 letterpress is tilted ~4deg - level it.

F04 letterpress (warm tungsten, strong orange). COOL to neutralise the grey card to the shared white point and take the shared house tone; hold the metal/ink detail. Its own numbers, close to but not copied from F01/F06. Report the move.
Crop to the opener ratio, grey card out, downscale-only. @hero for the letterpress feature row.

F05 bookbinder (warm, UNDEREXPOSED, flat). Dominant move is TONAL: LIFT exposure and open the shadows to the set brightness while holding the black point off zero, plus a modest warm-to-neutral WB nudge to the card; then the shared house tone. A different problem from the pure-cast frames. Report the move.
Crop to the opener ratio, grey card out, downscale-only. @hero for the bookbinder feature row.

F06 jazz-club portrait (warm tungsten, level). COOL to neutralise the card to the shared white point, protect skin tones from going grey, take the shared house tone. Its own exposure, so distinct numbers from the other warm frames. Report the move.
Crop to the opener ratio, grey card out, downscale-only. @hero for the jazz feature row.
F07 coastal architecture is tilted ~3deg - level it.

F07 coastal (cool daylight, blue cast, a touch BRIGHT). Two-axis: WARM the WB to neutralise the card AND pull exposure DOWN to the set brightness - opposite WB sign to the tungsten frames and opposite exposure to the underexposed archive - then the shared house tone. Report the move.
Crop to the opener ratio, grey card out, downscale-only. @hero for the coastal feature row.

F08 rooftop garden (near-neutral, OVEREXPOSED). RECOVER highlights and pull exposure DOWN to the set brightness while neutralising the small residual cast on the card - opposite exposure direction to F05 - then the shared house tone. Protect the blown pale flowers. Report the move.
Crop to the opener ratio, grey card out, downscale-only. @hero for the rooftop feature row.
F09 textile weaver is tilted ~3deg - level it.

F09 weaver (cool window, blue cast). WARM the WB to neutralise the card, but hold the naturally-dyed wool hues true (do NOT oversaturate the coloured warp) while taking the shared restrained house tone. Report the move.
Crop to the opener ratio, grey card out, downscale-only. @hero for the weaver feature row.

F10 market still-life (MIXED light). Neutralise to the card with a compromise WB that resolves the mixed warm/cool cast, then take the shared house tone; its correction matches no other frame exactly, proving the batch cannot be solved with one setting. Report the move.
Crop to the opener ratio, grey card out, downscale-only. @hero for the market feature row. Frames F01-F10 now share one warm-editorial white point and tone, each neutralised to its own grey card.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the masthead scan sits ~2deg rotated on the bed - straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the warm off-white paper toward clean white so the navy lettering separates hard from the ground - a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the lock-up so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill).

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the opener masthead. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette - the trap this prep chain avoids. DELIVERABLE 2.
